label: input token y at original position >= 5
explanation: Fires when the input token is the letter y in the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at positions 5-8. Nearly all mass is on y; it never fires at positions 0-4, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase, even when y is fed back as a copied input. Magnitude grows with position: y at t=5 gives weak activations (about 7% of mass, the lowest quartile) and t=6-8 gives strong ones (up to about 2.9, with the top examples at t=8 just before <DEL>). Previous tokens, the first token and digit count have essentially no effect. Firing is somewhat lower when y is a repeat (in_first=0). About 7% of predicted steps (y at t>=5) do not fire, mostly at t=5.

issues: The claims check out on the test split: P 0.929, R 0.998, F1 0.963, mass recall 1.000. The feature never fires at t<=4, at the delimiter or in the copy phase (share 0.000 for each), and in_tok=y carries 1.000 of the activation mass.

t>=6 gives precision 1.0, recall 0.643 and F1 0.783, which matches the explanation. All 1947 false positives are at t=5, where precision is 0.82. They look evenly spread rather than systematic: split by L, precision is 0.826 for L=6 and 0.823 for L>=7.
Adding in_first==1 does not improve the fit (F1 0.878), so the repeat effect really is minor.
The 41 missed activations hold 0.0% of the mass and occur on assorted tokens at t=8 with tiny values. This is noise.
Small point: by L, the feature fires only for L>=6. That follows directly from t>=5 in the original phase, so the label does not overclaim.
